data.one_liner: Annotations to express developer intentions for static analysis tools.
data.what_it_does: Provides annotations like @visibleForTesting, @immutable, and @sealed that static analysis tools use to analyze source code and check developer intentions. It also includes experimental annotations for dart2js.
use_when: You want to guide the Dart analyzer with custom metadata on classes, methods, or variables.
You are writing code that requires strict enforcement of architectural intentions such as mustCallSuper or immutable.
avoid_when: You need a general-purpose state management or UI library.
You are looking for runtime dependency injection frameworks.
strengths: Officially maintained by the Dart team.
Directly integrates with the Dart analyzer and IDE warnings.
weaknesses: Provides only annotations and no runtime logic or utilities.
Some hints/annotations may be experimental or change between minor versions.
data.setup_notes: Add package to dependencies in pubspec.yaml.
